rationale: The no-namespace half of the export surface, which cannot share a file with the namespaced half: C#'s file-scoped namespace applies to every declaration after it, so a file either has a namespace or does not. Two pins, and the second is the one that matters. (1) a `public` type at global scope IS exported, under its BARE name — `GlobalScopeType`, not `Acme.Anything.GlobalScopeType`, because the assembly has no namespace to qualify it with. (2) an `internal` type at global scope is NOT, which is the same visibility rule as the namespaced fixture and is pinned twice on purpose: a rule that is only tested inside a namespace is a rule whose behaviour outside one is unknown. Without this fixture the qualified-name change could have shipped a bare-name regression in the one case where a bare name is correct.

expectSymbols.name: GlobalScopeType
expectSymbols.note: no ownerName: a top-level type in a file with no namespace has no enclosing symbol

expectExports.name: GlobalScopeType
expectExports.comment: BARE, because there is no namespace to qualify with. The namespaced fixture pins the qualified spelling; this pins the unqualified one, and a rule that produced the qualified form here would be publishing a name the assembly does not export.

forbidRelationships.note: the visibility rule holds with no namespace in scope too
